title: Inside Out. Joy and Sadness.
lines: This is Riley.
Riley is an eleven-year-old girl.
She loves ice hockey, joking with her dad and her best friend.
But do you know what happens inside Riley's head?
Five little feelings live there!
They live in a big room with a control panel, full of buttons and lights.
From there they help Riley every day.
Joy is yellow and shines like the sun.
She's always laughing and bouncing around.
She's the boss.
Sadness is blue and small, with big glasses.
She's always a bit slow and she'd rather lie on the floor.
Anger is red and square.
When he gets angry, flames shoot out of his head.
Fear is purple and skinny.
He's scared of everything.
Watch out!
Danger!
And Disgust is green.
She thinks lots of things are yucky.
Yuck, broccoli!
Every time Riley experiences something, the panel makes a memory.
A little glass ball.
Happy memories are yellow.
Sad ones are blue.
Angry ones are red.
All the balls are stored on big shelves.
And the most important memories are in the middle.
They make Riley who she is.
One day Riley moves house with her mum and dad.
To a new city, far away.
The new house is small and dark.
Her room is bare.
There's a dead mouse in the corner.
The removal van is lost.
And at her new school she doesn't know anyone.
Inside Riley's head Joy is doing her best.
Come on, Riley!
Let's make it fun!
But Sadness keeps wanting to touch the memories.
And when she does, they turn blue.
Don't, Sadness!
shouts Joy.
On the first day of school Riley has to introduce herself to the class.
She talks about her old house.
And then Sadness touches a memory.
Riley starts to cry.
In front of the whole class.
Joy and Sadness have a fight.
They pull at the important memories.
And pop!
They both get sucked away.
Out of the room, far away in Riley's head.
Now only Anger, Fear and Disgust are left at the panel.
And they don't really know what to do.
Riley gets angry with her parents.
She doesn't want to play ice hockey anymore.
She isn't herself anymore.
Joy and Sadness have to get back.
They walk through Riley's head.
Through a land full of shelves of memories.
Through a theme park of imagination.
They meet Bing Bong.
He's Riley's imaginary friend from when she was little.
He's pink, part elephant, part cat, part dolphin, and he cries sweets.
Bing Bong helps them.
On the way something happens.
Bing Bong becomes sad, because Riley has forgotten him.
Joy tries to cheer him up.
Come on, Bing Bong!
Smile!
But it doesn't work.
Then Sadness sits down next to him.
She doesn't say anything.
She just listens.
That's really sad, she says softly.
You miss her.
Bing Bong cries a little.
And then he feels better.
Joy looks surprised.
Sadness could do something she couldn't.
Joy looks at an old memory.
Riley lost an important match.
She was very sad.
But then her mum and dad came.
They comforted her.
And her friends came.
And then Riley was happy again.
Now Joy understands.
When Riley is sad, the people who love her come to help her.
Sadness is important too!
Joy and Sadness finally get back to the room.
Joy hands the panel to Sadness.
You have to do it, she says.
Sadness touches the memories.
They turn blue.
And Riley goes to her mum and dad.
She starts to cry.
I miss our old house, she says.
I miss my friends.
Mum and Dad take her in their arms.
We miss it too, they say.
They cry together.
And they laugh together.
And then something lovely happens.
A new memory appears.
It's yellow and blue at the same time.
Happy and sad together.
Inside Riley's head the five feelings now work together.
And do you know what?
The feelings inside your head do too.
The end.
